title: LACE: Lattice Attention for Cross-thread Exploration in LLMs
claim: Independent samples collapse into the same flawed assumption; letting parallel threads communicate lets them pivot away from failures and find the correct answer.
layout: 2 panels side-by-side, bottom-to-top trees, green cross-thread arrows in right panel
description: Two side-by-side panels show the same math problem, a hyperbola rhombus question, in a gray box at the bottom of each. Reasoning threads branch upward as text boxes holding snippets of chain of thought. Each thread ends in a boxed final answer, drawn inside red concentric ellipses that stand for the solution space. Panel (a), Isolated samples fall into correlated failure modes, has three parallel threads. All three are tagged in red as an over-constrained assumption, and all reach the wrong answer 80. A green 480 sits off to the side, unreachable and crossed out. Panel (b), LACE explores diverse solutions, has threads linked by green curved arrows labeled Cross Thread Communication. Some threads are tagged as a similar failure and others as a pivot from failure paths. One thread reaches the green correct answer 480, marked with a check. Red marks for failure and green marks for success draw the eye first.
caption: Overcoming correlated failures in reasoning spaces. For complex problems, correct reasoning paths are often rare and widely separated. (a) Isolated Sampling: Standard parallel generation methods independently explore the space, frequently collapsing into correlated failure modes driven by shared, over-constrained assumptions. (b) LACE (Ours): By introducing latent cross-thread communication during generation, our method enables concurrent threads to actively pivot away from known failure paths. This shared context encourages the exploration of diverse reasoning modes, significantly increasing the probability of discovering the correct solution.
abstract: Current large language models reason in isolation. Although it is common to sample multiple reasoning paths in parallel, these trajectories do not interact, and often fail in the same redundant ways. We introduce LACE, a framework that transforms reasoning from a collection of independent trials into a coordinated, parallel process. By repurposing the model architecture to enable cross-thread attention, LACE allows concurrent reasoning paths to share intermediate insights and correct one another during inference. A central challenge is the absence of natural training data that exhibits such collaborative behavior. We address this gap with a synthetic data pipeline that explicitly teaches models to communicate and error-correct across threads. Experiments show that this unified exploration substantially outperforms standard parallel search, improving reasoning accuracy by over 7 points. Our results suggest that large language models can be more effective when parallel reasoning paths are allowed to interact.
